clue.text: Fun once hosted by Labour do

indicators.note: something hosted by other words sits inside them, so the letters are found within the phrase that follows

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and the whole of the second

explanation.surface: A Labour party gathering that offered some fun in the old days.
explanation.walkthrough: BOURD is an obsolete word for a jest; 'once' marks it as archaic.
explanation.definitionFit: Bourd is an old word for a jest or bit of merriment, which is what fun once meant.

clue.text: See band turning to round of applause in this informal do

blocks.clueFragment: See band turning to round of applause in this
blocks.note: surface reading: watch a musical group give way to clapping at a party

blocks.clueFragment: band turning to round of applause
blocks.note: setter's reading: the word band becomes hand (a round of applause) when its first letter B is read as H

explanation.surface: At this party, watch the band stop playing and the audience start clapping.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as B AS H: band turns into hand, a 'big hand' being a round of applause, once B is swapped for H.
explanation.definitionFit: A bash is a colloquial term for a party or celebration, an informal social do.

clue.text: Get the better of varied amount and love comic revue

indicators.note: varied means changed about, so the word before it is rearranged
something comic is clownish and jumbled, so the word after it is rearranged too

blocks.note: taken as written
love is nil in tennis, the letter O
taken as written

explanation.surface: A comic revue with a shifting budget and a romance manages to beat its rivals.
explanation.definitionFit: To outmanoeuvre someone is to outwit them by cleverer moves, getting the better of them.

clue.text: E.g. 22 going off, ruin pet

definitions.note: definition by example: a number written with repeated digits

indicators.note: food going off spoils and breaks down, so the letters that follow are reworked

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Twenty-two things going bad, wrecking a pet.
explanation.walkthrough: '22' looks like a cross-reference to another clue, but it is just a number given as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A repunit is a number made of repeated identical digits like 11 or 111; Azed stretches the example to 22.

clue.text: Kinder abroad, not at home, creating rubbish

indicators.note: not tells us the following phrase's letters are to be left out of the German word
abroad means scattered widely, so the remaining letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the German word for children, taken as written
at home is in

explanation.surface: Children overseas, out of the house, making a mess.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove IN from KINDER to leave KDER, then rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Drek is a Yiddish-derived word for trash or worthless stuff, i.e. rubbish.

clue.text: Grey panel disguised small anchor

indicators.note: something disguised has its appearance altered, so the word before it is rearranged

blocks.note: gr is an abbreviation for grey
taken as written

explanation.surface: A grey panel concealed a little anchor.
explanation.definitionFit: A grapnel is a small anchor with several flukes, used for boats or grappling.

clue.text: Fights breaking out, work in place that's busy at Xmas?

indicators.note: fights breaking out erupt chaotically, so that word's letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Brawls erupt at work in a shop crammed with Christmas customers.
explanation.definitionFit: A gift shop sells presents, so it is crowded in the run-up to Christmas; the question mark flags the definition by example.

clue.text: Indian manager, one from Chennai, say, first off, receiving upper class

indicators.note: first off means the opening letter is removed
receiving means taking something in, so the shortened word holds the next part

blocks.note: Chennai is in Tamil Nadu, so a native is a Tamil
U stands for upper class

explanation.surface: An Indian manager, a man from Chennai, gets a posh newcomer once the first one is gone.
explanation.walkthrough: TAMIL loses its T, then U goes in after the A.
explanation.definitionFit: An aumil (or amil) was a native revenue collector or agent in India, a kind of manager.

clue.text: Like a short course, second creating difficulty in the US

blocks.note: a short golf course has nine holes rather than eighteen
s is the abbreviation for second

explanation.surface: A short course, the second time round, causing trouble for an American golfer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Like a short course' looks like the definition, but it supplies the wordplay; American slang 'in the nine-holes' means in a fix.
explanation.definitionFit: In US usage, to be in the nine-holes is to be in trouble, so the word names a predicament.

clue.text: One making inferences, unusually inferior, about karzy

indicators.note: about means placed around, so the word for inferior wraps the lavatory term

blocks.note: extra as an adverb means unusually, as in extra large
poor means inferior in quality
karzy is British slang for a toilet; lat is short for latrine

explanation.surface: Someone drawing conclusions, oddly second-rate, about the lavatory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusually' looks like an anagram signal but supplies a word of its own; karzy is British slang for a toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: To extrapolate is to infer beyond known data, so an extrapolator is a person who draws such inferences.

clue.text: Five years denied strong drink, one shares quality with 28

indicators.note: denied means refused, so the spirit is taken away from the period

blocks.note: a lustrum is a five-year period
rum is a strong spirit

explanation.surface: Five teetotal years for someone who shares a trait with another clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 28 is AVARICE; both are among the seven deadly sins.
explanation.definitionFit: Lust and avarice are two of the seven deadly sins, so lust shares that sinful quality.

clue.text: An addict that is given preference to wife? It's no joke (9, two words)

definitions.note: the answer is an adverbial phrase meaning seriously; the clue phrase stands for treating something as no joke

indicators.note: given preference means placed ahead, so the abbreviation for that is comes before the one for wife

blocks.note: taken as the article
a user is a drug addict
ie is the abbreviation of id est, that is
ux is the abbreviation of Latin uxor, wife

explanation.surface: An addict who is favoured over his wife: not funny.
explanation.definitionFit: French au sérieux means seriously, as in taking something au sérieux: treating it as no laughing matter.

clue.text: Underground excavation to plug end of mine

indicators.note: end of points to the final letter of the next word only

blocks.note: to stop a hole is to plug it
the last letter of mine

explanation.surface: Digging below ground to seal off the far end of a mine.
explanation.definitionFit: A stope is a step-like excavation in a mine from which ore is removed underground.

clue.text: Applies poultice to chaps in soft liquid

indicators.note: in places the men inside the reworked letters
liquid means fluid and shifting, so the word before it is rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
chaps are men

explanation.surface: A nurse dressing some men's wounds while they soak in a gentle bath.
explanation.definitionFit: To foment is, in its medical sense, to bathe with warm lotions or apply hot compresses.

clue.text: Surgical transplant, with the author's own hand, we hear?

indicators.note: we hear signals a word that is only spoken like the one described

blocks.note: a signed copy is autographed, signed in the writer's own hand

explanation.surface: A transplant operation, signed off personally by the writer.
explanation.definitionFit: An autograft is tissue moved from one part of a patient's body to another, a transplant within one person.

clue.text: Scots pickled cheesecake maybe I have stuffed

indicators.note: something stuffed has a filling put inside, so the pastry holds the contraction

blocks.note: a cheesecake is an example of a tart

explanation.walkthrough: 'Pickled' looks like cookery but is slang for drunk, and 'Scots' marks the dialect word.
explanation.definitionFit: Taivert is Scots for muddled or fuddled, especially with drink, just as pickled means drunk.

clue.text: One often portrayed in kirk, special one often sainted?

blocks.note: s is an abbreviation for special
the exclamation 'my sainted aunt!' makes an aunt the relative often called sainted

explanation.surface: A holy figure seen in church pictures, a special sort of person.
explanation.walkthrough: A kirk is a Scottish church, which signals the Scots spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Saunt is Scots for saint, and saints are frequently depicted in church windows and paintings.

clue.text: Green and tasty, possibly with a bit of grey in?

indicators.note: a bit of keeps just the opening letter of the colour word
in places that single letter inside the word for possibly

blocks.note: say means for instance, possibly
the first letter of grey

explanation.surface: Something green and flavourful, perhaps with a touch of grey.
explanation.definitionFit: Sagy means full of or flavoured with sage, a grey-green herb, so it is both green and tasty.

clue.text: Keep what's appropriate to part of coiffure

blocks.note: something meant for a purpose is suited to it
a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: Retain whatever suits a section of your hairdo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keep' looks like a verb; it is the noun for a castle stronghold.
explanation.definitionFit: A keep is the strongest tower of a castle, a stronghold, so a fortress.

clue.text: It descends to a river partly through a tunnel

indicators.note: partly means only part of the following words is used, the letters sitting within them

blocks.note: the letters straddle all three words

explanation.surface: A path that goes down to the riverbank, part of it through a tunnel.
explanation.definitionFit: In India a ghat is a flight of steps leading down to a river landing place.

clue.text: Excessively long utensil

blocks.note: too means excessively
l is the abbreviation for long

explanation.surface: A kitchen implement that is far too lengthy.
explanation.definitionFit: A utensil is an implement or instrument, which is what a tool is.

clue.text: Piece of church music, end bit, hard, soon coming round

blocks.note: anon means soon
a tip is an end bit
h is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A choir piece with a hard final bit, coming round again shortly.
explanation.definitionFit: An antiphon is a short chant sung responsively in church services, a piece of church music.

clue.text: Good car model in centres of activity

blocks.note: g is the abbreviation for good
the Ford Anglia was a British car model

explanation.surface: A fine car model to be found where the action is.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ford Anglia was a small family car made in Britain from the 1940s to the 1960s.
explanation.definitionFit: A ganglion is a nerve cell cluster and, figuratively, a centre of energy or activity.

clue.text: Left potato in temporary privy

blocks.note: port is the left side of a ship
aloo is the Hindi word for potato, familiar from Indian menus

explanation.surface: A potato abandoned in a portable toilet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a container signal but just joins wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Portaloo is a British trade name for a portable toilet, a privy set up temporarily at events.

clue.text: Cracksman having yen to introduce bomb

egg is old slang for a bomb

clue.text: Hot wind? One follows mostly cold spell

clue.text: What angler fixes to hook, making contact from behind line

clue.text: Magic herb making one relax, life mostly passing

clue.text: What's this, involving a bit of rapacity?
